summary_paragraph: A woman with sickle cell disease and chronic hepatitis C was admitted for her second cycle of adjuvant doxorubicin and cisplatin chemotherapy for high-grade osteosarcoma of the left tibia. She had previously experienced severe delayed nausea, dehydration, and syncope after cycle one, requiring hospitalization. This admission was elective and uncomplicated; she tolerated chemotherapy well with only mild nausea and a resolving dry cough. Her labs showed mild anemia, for which she received a red blood cell transfusion prior to discharge, and reactive thrombocytosis. Liver enzymes remained mildly elevated, attributed to chemotherapy, hepatitis C, and sickle cell disease, but hepatology approved continuation of treatment. She was discharged on scheduled antiemetics, including a dexamethasone taper, and instructions to begin Neupogen injections the following morning to mitigate neutropenia risk. Follow-up was arranged, with emphasis on hydration, infection monitoring, and adherence to anti-nausea regimen.
problems: Chronic hepatitis C without mention of hepatic coma
Cirrhosis of liver without mention of alcohol
Malignant neoplasm of long bones of lower limb
Nonspecific elevation of levels of transaminase or lactic acid dehydrogenase [LDH]
